words: أَسْكَنتُ مِن ذُرِّيَّتِى بِوَادٍ غَيْرِ ذِى زَرْعٍ عِندَ بَيْتِكَ ٱلْمُحَرَّمِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham says he settled some descendants beside the sanctified Temple in an uncultivable valley so they could devote themselves to prayer.
rows.anchor: Behold, I have settled some of my offspring

words: فَٱجْعَلْ أَفْـِٔدَةًۭ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهْوِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ وَٱرْزُقْهُم مِّنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks that people's hearts incline toward his family and that they receive fruitful sustenance, enabling gratitude.
rows.anchor: cause Thou, therefore, people's hearts to incline towards them [53] and grant them fruitful sustenance

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The valley is Mecca's narrow desert valley, enclosed by barren, rocky hills.
rows.anchor: the narrow desert valley of Mecca, which is enclosed by barren, rocky hills

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's offspring here means Ishmael and his descendants, who settled at Mecca.
rows.anchor: Abraham refers to Ishmael and his descendants who settled at Mecca

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asad reads the phrase as people's desire to visit Abraham's family on pilgrimage, thereby helping them live in the holy but barren land.
rows.anchor: to be desirous of visiting them - namely, on pilgrimage to Mecca - and thus help them to maintain themselves in the holy but barren land

rows.speaker: Baghawi, Razi, Ibn Kathir
rows.claim: Baghawi, Razi, and Ibn Kathir allow the phrase to mean the hearts of some people, understood as believers' hearts.
rows.anchor: Baghawi, Razi, Ibn Kathir

words: إِنَّكَ تَعْلَمُ مَا نُخْفِى وَمَا نُعْلِنُ
وَمَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍۢ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham acknowledges that God knows what is hidden inwardly and what is public, and that nothing on earth or in heaven is concealed from Him.
rows.anchor: Thou truly knowest all that we may hide [in our hearts] as well as all that we bring into the open

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham praises God for granting him Ishmael and Isaac in his old age and affirms that God hears prayer.
rows.anchor: who has bestowed upon me, in my old age, Ishmael and Isaac! Behold, my Sustainer hears indeed all prayer

words: رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْنِى مُقِيمَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks God to keep him and some of his descendants constant in prayer.
rows.anchor: cause me and [some] of my offspring to remain constant in prayer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks forgiveness for himself, his parents, and all believers on the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: Grant Thy forgiveness unto me, and my parents, and all the believers, on the Day on which the [last] reckoning will come to pass

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Establish prayer” is metonymic for remaining utterly devoted to God.
rows.anchor: metonymically, "to remain utterly devoted to Thee"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “some of my offspring” alludes to 2:124: Abraham understands that some descendants will be evildoers, so lineage cannot make anyone a chosen person. This applies to Israelite and Ishmaelite branches, including Quraysh and unrighteous descendants of Muhammad.
rows.anchor: is obviously an allusion to 2:124, where God says in answer to Abraham's question about his descendants

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following discussion connects with Abraham's closing prayer for the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: the last sentence of Abraham's prayer, namely, his reference to "the Day on which the [last] reckoning will come to pass"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are those who believe other powers rival God, committing shirk, which Asad calls unforgivable; he links this to 14:30.
rows.anchor: those who indulge in the belief "that there are other powers that can rival God" (cf. verse 30 above), and thus commit the unforgivable sin of shirk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the respite given to wrongdoers, Asad refers to 11:20 and its corresponding note 39.
rows.anchor: As regards the "respite" granted to them, see the first clause of 11:20 and the corresponding note 39

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are to be warned of the day punishment befalls them, when wrongdoers will beg for a short delay so they can answer God's call and follow the apostles.
rows.anchor: warn men of the Day when this suffe ring may befall them

words: أَوَلَمْ تَكُونُوٓا۟ أَقْسَمْتُم مِّن قَبْلُ مَا لَكُم مِّن زَوَالٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers that they had earlier sworn no resurrection and retribution awaited them; the next verse recalls lessons from prior sinful peoples and parables already given.
rows.anchor: were you not aforetime wont to swear that no kind of resurrection and retribution awaited you?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their own residence among earlier sinful peoples and the examples and parables of their fate had made the warning clear.
rows.anchor: And yet, you dwelt in the dwelling-places of those who had sinned against their own selves [before your time]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asad points to 6:27 as a parallel for the wrongdoers' plea to return and respond to God's call.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The literal image is no “going down” or removal: no passage from earthly life to the hereafter and its retribution, reflecting the Qur'anic rejection of afterlife and final judgment by many.
rows.anchor: Lit., "that there would be no going down [or "no removal"] whatever for you"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers address the Prophet as one who allegedly received the reminder from on high and call him mad.
rows.anchor: O thou unto whom this reminder has [allegedly] been bestowed from on high: verily, thou art mad

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They challenge the Prophet to produce angels as proof of his truthfulness.
rows.anchor: Why dost thou not bring before us angels, if thou art a man of truth?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels are sent only in accordance with truth; if they appeared at the deniers' demand, those rejecters would receive no further respite.
rows.anchor: We never send down angels otherwise than in accordance with the [demands of] truth;

words: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا ٱلذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَٰفِظُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says that He revealed the reminder in stages and will preserve it from corruption.
rows.anchor: this reminder? and, behold, it is We who shall truly guard it [from all corruption]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder is the Qur'an; the form nazzalna indicates gradual revelation, as Zamakhshari notes on 2:23 and Asad's note 14 there explains.
rows.anchor: I.e., the Qur'an. The grammatical form nazzalnd implies a gradual revelation ("step by step") over a period of time

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asad says the prophecy is confirmed by the Qur'an's unchanged text since the seventh century, and claims no other book has been preserved similarly for so long.
rows.anchor: the text of the Qur'an has remained free from all alterations, additions or deletions ever since it was enunciated by the Prophet in the seventh century

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Early variants reported by classical commentators concern diacritical marks or vocalization and generally do not change meaning; Asad also refers to lawh mahfuz in 85:22.
rows.anchor: differences in respect of diacritical marks or of vocalisation, and, as a rule, do not affect the meaning of the passage in question

words: فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُۥ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forms mortal man fully, breathes spirit into him, and commands the angels to prostrate before him.
rows.anchor: when I have formed him fully and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down before him in prostration

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation and prostration passages are allegorical: God's creation requires no elapsed time, since His will brings a thing into being immediately, as several verses affirm.
rows.anchor: the allegorical character of all the passages bearing on the creation of man and on God's command to the angels to prostrate themselves before him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's breathing of His spirit is a metaphor for endowing man with life and consciousness, that is, with a soul.
rows.anchor: God's "breathing of His spirit" into man is obviously a metaphor for His endowing him with life and consciousness: that is, with a soul

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creator cannot be equated with beings unable to create, a contrast meant to prompt reflection.
rows.anchor: IS, THEN, HE who creates comparable to any [being] that cannot create?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's blessings cannot be counted, and He is forgiving and gracious.
rows.anchor: For, should you try to count God's blessings, you could never compute them! Behold, God is indeed much-forgiving, a dispenser of grace

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what people conceal and what they disclose.
rows.anchor: God knows all that you keep secret as well as all that you bring into the open

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those invoked beside God are themselves created and cannot create anything.
rows.anchor: Now those beings that some people invoke [13] beside God cannot create anything, since they themselves are but created

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These beings are dead rather than alive and do not know when they will be resurrected.
rows.anchor: they are dead, not living, [14] and they do not [even] know when they will be raised from the dead

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invoked beings are dead saints whom followers have given divine or semi-divine qualities.
rows.anchor: this refers - as is obvious from verse 21 below - to dead saints invested by their followers with divine or semi-divine qualities

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should not trade their bond with God for a small worldly gain, since what is with God is far better.
rows.anchor: do not barter away your bond with God for a trifling gain! Verily, that which is with God is by far the best for you

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What people possess passes away, whereas what is with God endures.
rows.anchor: all that is with you is bound to come to an end, whereas that which is with God is everlasting

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises the patient in adversity a reward according to the best of their deeds.
rows.anchor: most certainly shall We grant unto those who are patient in adversity their reward in accordance with the best that they ever did

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic ethical discipline does not constrict life; it deepens awareness of right and wrong and thereby enhances life.
rows.anchor: the ethical discipline imposed upon man by the teachings of the Qur'an is not meant to narrow down his feel of life, but, on the contrary, to enhance it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in the heavens, on earth, between them, and beneath the soil belongs to God.
rows.anchor: Unto Him belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on earth, as well as all that is between them and all that is beneath the sod

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows even what is hidden within people, whether they speak aloud or not.
rows.anchor: if thou say anything aloud, [He hears it - ] since, behold, He knows [even] the secret [thoughts of man] as well as all that is yet more hidden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows both unspoken conscious thoughts and what takes place in the subconscious.
rows.anchor: He knows not only man's unspoken, conscious thoughts but also all that goes on within his subconscious self

words: إِنَّنِىٓ أَنَا ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God declares that He alone is God and commands worship of Him alone; prayer's purpose is remembrance of Him.
rows.anchor: Verily, I - I alone - am God; there is no de ity save Me. Hence, worship Me alone

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though God has kept the Last Hour hidden, it will come so every person may be recompensed for what they strove for.
rows.anchor: Behold, [although] I have willed to keep it[11] hidden, the Last Hour is bound to come

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conscious remembrance of God's oneness and uniqueness is both the innermost purpose and the intellectual justification of all true prayer.
rows.anchor: conscious remembrance of God and of His oneness and uniqueness is declared to be the innermost purpose, as well as the intellectual justification of all true prayer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is warned not to let someone who disbelieves in the Hour and follows desire divert him from belief in it.
rows.anchor: Hence, let not anyone who does not believe in its coming [13] and follows [but] his own desires divert thee

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God asks Moses what he is holding in his right hand.
rows.anchor: Now, what is this in thy right hand, O Moses?

words: قَالَ هِىَ عَصَاىَ أَتَوَكَّؤُا۟ عَلَيْهَا وَأَهُشُّ بِهَا عَلَىٰ غَنَمِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses uses his staff to lean on and beat leaves for his sheep, among other purposes.
rows.anchor: It is my staff; I lean on it; a nd with it I beat down leaves for my sheep

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Moses to cast down the staff, and it becomes a rapidly moving snake.
rows.anchor: Said He: "Throw it down, O Moses!"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Moses to take the snake without fear and promises to restore the staff to its original state.
rows.anchor: Take hold of it, and fear not: We shall restore it to its former state

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is given a second sign: his hand emerges white without blemish, to make him aware of God's great wonders.
rows.anchor: Now place thy hand within thy armpit: it will come forth [shining] white, without blemish

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asad reads the staff's transformation mystically as an allusion to appearance versus reality and the spiritual insight God grants chosen servants; Moses' encounter with the unnamed sage and the wording in 27:10 and 28:31 support this reading.
rows.anchor: the staff into a serpent has, I believe, a mystic significance: it seems to be an allusion to the intrinsic difference between appearance and reality

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks God to open his heart to divine light.
rows.anchor: O my Sustainer! Open up my heart [to Thy light]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks God to make his task easy.
rows.anchor: make my task easy for me

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks for clear speech and Aaron's help, strength, and shared work so they can glorify and remember God; he affirms that God sees their inner state.
rows.anchor: Add Thou through him to my strength, (20:32) and let him share my task

words: مِنْهَا خَلَقْنَٰكُمْ وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمْ وَمِنْهَا نُخْرِجُكُمْ تَارَةً أُخْرَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man's body is created from earth and returns to it by dissolving into its elementary organic and inorganic substances; creation, life, and dissolution show God's power, life's ephemerality, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: its "return into it" signifies the dissolution of this body, after death, into the elementary organic and inorganic substances of which it was composed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses warns them not to invent lies against God, lest grievous suffering strike them; a fabricator is already doomed.
rows.anchor: Woe unto you! Do not invent lies against God, [43] lest He afflict you

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inventing lies against God means deliberately denying the truth of His messages.
rows.anchor: by deliberately denying the truth of His messages

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents confer secretly and accuse Moses and Aaron of sorcery aimed at driving them from their land and destroying their inherited way of life.
rows.anchor: These two are surely so rcerers intent on driving you from your land [44] by their sorcery

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They urge the assembled sorcerers to decide on a scheme and present themselves together, declaring that the victor will prosper.
rows.anchor: you will pursue, and then come forward in one single body

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The literal “in one line” means that they should act in unison.
rows.anchor: Lit., "in one [single] line", i.e., in unison

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asad compares this contest's call for unified action with the magicians' assembly in 7:113-114.

words: لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ وَٱلَّذِى فَطَرَنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians refuse to prefer Pharaoh over clear proofs and their Creator, accepting that Pharaoh can decree only for this worldly life.
rows.anchor: Never shall we prefer thee to all the evidence of the truth that has come unto us, nor to Him who has brought us into being! Decree, then, whatever thou art going to decree

words: إِنَّآ ءَامَنَّا بِرَبِّنَا لِيَغْفِرَ لَنَا خَطَٰيَٰنَا وَمَآ أَكْرَهْتَنَا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلسِّحْرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They profess faith and seek forgiveness for their faults and the magic Pharaoh had forced them to practice, trusting in God's superior and abiding goodness.
rows.anchor: we have come to believe in our Sustainer, [hoping] that He may forgive us our faults

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb qada can mean either “decree” or “end”; the magicians may mean Pharaoh can end only their worldly life.
rows.anchor: the verb qada signifies, among other meanings, "he decreed" as well as "he ended [something]"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh, the title of Egypt's indigenous rulers, was a god-king and embodiment of Egyptian religion, where magic was central; subjects were expected to accept it as part of life.
rows.anchor: Pharaoh (a title borne by every indigenous ruler of Egypt) was considered to be a "god-king" and, thus, the embodiment of the Egyptian religion

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase literally means “the most abiding,” that is, eternal; Asad refers to 55:26-27.
rows.anchor: Lit., "and the most abiding", i.e., eternal

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sinner who appears before God faces Hell, where he neither dies nor lives.
rows.anchor: VERILY, as for him who shall appear before his Sustainer [on Judgment Day] lost in sin - his [portion], behold, shall be hell

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who do good receive lofty stations and eternal gardens with flowing waters; this is the reward of those who attain purity.
rows.anchor: whereas he who shall appear before Him as a belie ver who has done righteous deeds [59]

rows.speaker: Baghawi, Baydawi
rows.claim: Baghawi and Baydawi explain that the condemned neither undergo spiritual rebirth nor find peace through extinction.
rows.anchor: he will neither be reborn spiritually nor find peace through extinction (Baghawi, Baydawi)

rows.speaker: Baydawi
rows.claim: Baydawi identifies the term mu'mim in this context with someone who consciously and persistently denied God during life, contrasting it with mu'min in the next verse.
rows.anchor: the former term is here applied to one who, in his lifetime, has consciously and persistently denied God (Baydawi)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted as Ultimate Sovereign and Ultimate Truth.
rows.anchor: the Ultimate Sovereign, the Ultimate Truth

words: وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِٱلْقُرْءَانِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told not to hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is complete.
rows.anchor: and [knowing this,] do not approach the Qur'an in haste, [100] ere it has been revealed unto thee in full

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse directs the Prophet to pray for increased knowledge.
rows.anchor: [always) say: "O my Sustainer, cause me to grow in knowledge!"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When al-haqq designates God, it means absolute, intrinsic truth that exists eternally and immutably beyond creation's changing phenomena.
rows.anchor: it signifies "the Truth" in the absolute, intrinsic sense, eternally and immutably existing beyond the ephemeral, changing phenomena of His creation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-malik denotes God's absolute sway over all existence and is rendered “Ultimate Sovereign.”
rows.anchor: God's attribute of al-malik, on the other hand, denotes His absolute sway over all that exists

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asad gives the literal rendering “be not hasty with the Qur'an” and points to the following note for explanation.
rows.anchor: Lit., "be not hasty with the Qur'an" (see next note)
